findings.text: A tmpfs inode wrapper is anchored by an embedded generic inode with a helper that recovers the outer record from that member. The outer record keeps NUMA guidance and creation time plus extended attribute linkage and ioctl flag storage and a fallocate high water mark. Separately it tracks seal state and general flags and tallies for resident versus swapped out contents and a hold that suspends eviction during work. One shared union has two personalities by file kind, either durable directory positioning or linkage for reclaimable huge pages and swap candidates. Extra quota pointers exist only under a quota build.

A tmpfs superblock record holds capacity and usage for blocks and inodes with free space tracking and per cpu accounting, mount identity and mode, huge page preference, swap avoidance, and full inode number selection. Inode numbering uses a global next value plus a per cpu batch. It also stores a default memory policy and an extended attribute cache and default quota limits for users and groups covering block and inode hard ceilings. Reclaim linkage includes a list with its length.

Tmpfs uses a per inode spin guard and a per filesystem raw guard described as serializing superblock statistic changes and a separate per filesystem spin guard described as protecting the reclaimable inode list. Eviction control uses an atomic hold taken while operating on an inode. Block usage uses a per cpu counter rather than a plain integer.

Three tmpfs file flags occupy successive low bit positions for no reserve and locked and frozen mapping. Three flag groups select user visibility and user mutability and inheritance from underlying filesystem flag facets including immutability and append and dump avoidance and access time avoidance and case folding. Both space and inode quota ceilings equal the largest positive signed 63 bit value.

Page acquisition intent has five ordered modes. One only serves data already within file size without creating storage. A second is similar but treats missing coverage as failure while honoring previously reserved coverage. A third stays within size yet may create storage. A fourth may grow beyond size and may return storage not yet marked current. A fifth behaves like growth but marks preexisting storage current.

In the routed build several tmpfs queries are constant. Mapping identification is always negative, allowable huge orders are empty, huge PMD enablement is negative, swap accounting is zero, and uncharging does nothing. Folio and page readers forward to GFP variants using the address space allocation mask. A file test first honors a disabled shared memory build, then rejects absent objects or mappings, then defers to mapping identification.

Freezing toggles the frozen mapping flag on the inode wrapper while leaving other flags intact. The fallocate horizon query returns the greater of the supplied end and the stored horizon. Wrapper recovery from a generic inode relies on container address arithmetic around the embedded member.

Swap token layout splits a compact value into a type field and an offset field. The shift width is derived from abstract value capacity minus swap file index capacity, and the offset mask covers exactly that low width. Frame number width has two configurations, one derived from physical address capacity minus page shift and another capped by both native address width and the type shift. Its mask covers that width. Two access versus dirtiness bits sit immediately above the frame field with a total spanning both.
Conversion between an abstract collection value and a swap token preserves the numeric payload in both directions, so a round trip yields the original token.

Device private and migration token makers have feature present and feature absent forms. When present they tag a supplied offset with distinct kinds for readable and writable device use and exclusive device use and for readable and exclusive readable and writable migration. Youth and dirtiness setters add the corresponding high bits only where access and dirtiness tracking is supported and otherwise leave the token unchanged. When absent the same makers yield a zero token and migration waits do nothing.

Hardware poison handling has present and absent forms. When present creation requires a locked input page and encodes its frame number under a poison kind, and testing compares the kind field for equality. When absent creation yields a zero token and testing is always negative.
A page table marker is an unsigned scalar with three distinct low positions for write protection notification and poisoned state and guard state. A combined mask covers exactly those three positions.
Marker token creation tags a marker payload with a dedicated marker kind, and page table creation wraps that token. Poisoned and guard helpers are thin specializations supplying the matching payload.

Compound migration installation and removal for huge mappings are compile time traps in the routed configuration and must not be invoked there, while the compound wait is empty. Poison token creation asserts that its input page is locked, so calling it unlocked triggers a bug trap.

A userfaultfd context centers on four notification queues for not yet consumed faults and faults generally and descriptor polling and events. It carries syscall flags and negotiated features and a released marker and a target address space pointer. Change tracking uses a refile sequence number plus a changing count plus a read write guard that separates outside address space mutation from fault resolution operations. Lifetime uses a reference count.

Filesystem support for userfaultfd is a table of five operations. One decides whether an area can participate. One looks up an already cached locked referenced folio without allocating. One allocates a fresh folio for a copy resolution. One inserts such a folio into the cache for an address and reports status. One undoes that insertion on error paths.

Userfaultfd context synchronization separates concerns. The pending fault queue lock also orders the refile sequence. Reference counting governs descriptor lifetime. A read write semaphore is taken in write mode for outside changes and in read mode for fault fill and move and protection operations that sample the changing indicator. An atomic count records that outside mutation is in progress.

Userfaultfd mode coverage combines missing handling with minor handling and with write protection and remote write protection, expressed once for legacy flags and once for area masks. Shared descriptor creation combines close on exec with nonblocking behavior. Operation flags use a distinct bitwise unsigned type so mode and flag bits do not mix with plain integers.

Atomic fill has four modes for copying contents and clearing to zero and continuing from cache and poisoning, plus a count sentinel. Mode width is sized from that count, flag positions start above the mode field, a mask isolates the mode, and write protection is the first flag. Helpers test whether flags carry an expected mode and replace the mode while preserving flags.

When enabled, area compatibility compares attached contexts for identity. Sharing of huge mappings and read around are suppressed where write protection or remote protection or minor handling is armed. Separate predicates report missing and minor and remote protection, with remote protection folded negative without architecture protection none support. Combined protection is either write or remote form. Armed means any mode is present. Entry level write and remote states require both area mode and entry marking. Marker use is required for file protection and for anonymous protection only with unpopulated tracking, which is negative here. Swap entry relevance requires marker support and absence of presence plus either entry marking or marker form.

When disabled the fault path is inert. Synchronous fault entry reports a bus error and range protection reports failure. All mode and entry predicates report negative except merge compatibility which reports affirmative. Duplication and remap preparation and completion and failure and removal and unmap preparation and completion succeed trivially or do nothing. Asynchronous protection queries and remap event queries and marker use queries are negative.
